app.name: coscene
ui.locked_scene: Solve the scene before this one first.
ui.hint_none: That was the last hint for this scene.
ui.notebook_empty: Ideas you uncover are kept here.
ui.reset_body: Your stars, hints, notebook and score will be cleared. This can't be undone.
ui.privacy: coscene collects no data and works offline.
ui.profile_score_note: cosIQ is a game score from the scenes you solve. It is not a measured IQ.
ui.profile_share_text: My cosIQ is {score}. Can you beat it? #coscene
card.caption: Logic, maths and algorithms, solved by hand
place.daily.name: Daily scene
place.binary.name: Binary
place.binary.tagline: Numbers made of ones and zeros
scene.binary.from_binary.objective: What number do these bits make?
hint.binary.1: Each bit is worth double the one to its right.
hint.binary.2: Start with the biggest place value that still fits, then fill in what is left.
hint.binary.3: Write the number as a sum of 8, 4, 2 and 1 (and more places for bigger numbers).
concept.binary.name: Place value in base 2
concept.binary.idea: Each bit is a power of two. A number in binary is the sum of the powers whose bits are 1.
concept.binary.seen: Memory, file sizes, network masks, every integer a computer stores
reveal.binary: You built the number from powers of two.
place.bitwise.name: Bitwise operators
scene.bitwise.combine.objective: Combine a and b bit by bit. What number comes out?
scene.bitwise.shift.objective: Shift the bits of a. What number comes out?
hint.bitwise.1: Line the two rows up and look at one column at a time.
hint.bitwise.2: AND keeps a 1 only where both have 1. OR keeps a 1 where either has one. XOR keeps a 1 where they differ.
hint.bitwise.3: A shift left by one doubles the number; a shift right by one halves it, dropping the remainder.
concept.bitwise.name: Bitwise operators
concept.bitwise.idea: Bitwise operators work on every bit position at once, without carries between columns.
concept.bitwise.seen: Flags and permissions, fast multiply and divide by two, graphics, hashing
reveal.bitwise: You worked through it one bit column at a time.
place.logic.name: Logic
place.logic.tagline: True, false and the operators between them
scene.logic.evaluate.objective: Is each expression true or false?
hint.logic.1: Replace each letter with its value first.
hint.logic.2: && is true only when both sides are true. || is true when at least one side is. ! flips true and false.
hint.logic.3: Work inside the brackets first, then the ! signs, then && before ||.
concept.logic.name: Boolean logic
concept.logic.idea: Every condition in a program boils down to true or false, combined with and, or and not.
concept.logic.seen: if statements, search filters, database WHERE clauses, circuit design
reveal.logic: You evaluated each condition step by step.
place.logarithms.name: Logarithms
place.logarithms.tagline: How many times you multiply or halve
scene.logarithms.halvings.objective: You keep halving {n}, rounding up. How many halvings until you reach 1?
hint.logarithms.1: log₂ x asks: two to what power gives x?
hint.logarithms.2: Count how many times you can divide by the base before you reach 1.
hint.logarithms.3: ⌊ ⌋ rounds down and ⌈ ⌉ rounds up. log of a product is the sum of the logs.
concept.logarithms.name: Logarithms
concept.logarithms.idea: A logarithm counts how many times you multiply by the base. log₂ n is how many halvings shrink n to 1.
concept.logarithms.seen: Why binary search takes about log n steps, sorting costs n log n, tree heights
reveal.logarithms: You counted the doublings hiding in the number.
place.counting.name: Counting
scene.counting.line_up.objective: In how many different orders can {n} friends stand in a line?
scene.counting.outfits.objective: You have {a} shirts and {b} trousers. How many different outfits can you wear?
scene.counting.podium.objective: {n} runners race. In how many ways can the first {k} places be filled?
scene.counting.team.objective: In how many ways can you pick a team of {k} from {n} people?
hint.counting.1: Count the choices for each step, one step at a time.
hint.counting.2: When steps happen together, multiply the number of choices. n! is n × (n − 1) × … × 1.
hint.counting.3: Order matters: P(n, k) = n × (n − 1) × … for k terms. Order does not matter: divide that by k!.
concept.counting.name: Permutations and combinations
concept.counting.idea: Multiply the choices at each step. If order does not matter, divide by the ways to reorder what you picked.
concept.counting.seen: Counting test cases, password strength, how fast brute force grows
reveal.counting: You multiplied the choices, step by step.
place.modulo.name: Modulo
scene.modulo.clock.objective: It is {h} o’clock. What time will the clock show {k} hours from now?
scene.modulo.last_digit.objective: What is the last digit of {b} to the power {k}?
hint.modulo.1: a mod m is what is left after taking away as many m as you can.
hint.modulo.2: Clocks wrap around every 12 hours, so only the remainder after dividing by 12 matters.
hint.modulo.3: Last digits repeat in a short cycle. Find the cycle length, then use the power mod that length.
concept.modulo.name: Modular arithmetic
concept.modulo.idea: Modulo keeps only the remainder, so values wrap around in a fixed range.
concept.modulo.seen: Hash tables, circular buffers, clocks and calendars, cryptography
reveal.modulo: You let the numbers wrap around.
place.binary_search.name: Binary search
scene.binary_search.compare.objective: A number from 1 to {hi} is hidden. Pin it down in {budget} checks.
scene.binary_search.bisect.objective: One version from 1 to {hi} broke the build, and every later one is broken too. Find the first bad one in {budget} checks.
hint.binary_search.1: Each answer rules out one side. Make both sides the same size.
hint.binary_search.2: Always check the middle of what is still possible.
hint.binary_search.3: With n numbers left, the middle check leaves at most half. That is why it takes about log₂ n checks.
concept.binary_search.name: Binary search
concept.binary_search.idea: Check the middle of a sorted range and throw away the half that cannot hold the answer.
concept.binary_search.seen: Searching sorted data, git bisect, database indexes, finding a bug by halving
reveal.binary_search: You halved the range every time.
place.two_pointers.name: Two pointers
scene.two_pointers.pair_sum.objective: Pick the two tiles that add up to {target}.
hint.two_pointers.1: The row is sorted. Start with the smallest and the largest.
hint.two_pointers.2: Too big? Move the right end in. Too small? Move the left end in.
hint.two_pointers.3: Each step rules out one tile for good, so you never check a pair twice.
concept.two_pointers.name: Two pointers
concept.two_pointers.idea: On sorted data, two ends that move towards each other find a pair in one pass.
concept.two_pointers.seen: Two sum, merging sorted lists, removing duplicates in place
reveal.two_pointers: You walked in from both ends.
place.stacks.name: Stacks
scene.stacks.stack.objective: Items arrive in order. Use the stack to send them out in the target order.
scene.stacks.stack_cap.objective: Items arrive in order. Send them out in the target order. The stack holds at most {cap}.
hint.stacks.1: Only the top of the stack can come out.
hint.stacks.2: Push until the item you need next is on top, then pop it.
hint.stacks.3: If the item you need is buried under others, that order is impossible, so plan ahead.
concept.stacks.name: Stacks
concept.stacks.idea: A stack only lets you take the most recent item. Last in, first out.
concept.stacks.seen: Undo, the call stack, checking brackets, browser back buttons
reveal.stacks: Last in, first out, worked out by hand.
place.queues.name: Queues
scene.queues.front.objective: → adds to the back and ← takes from the front. Who is at the front at the end?
scene.queues.front_size.objective: → adds to the back and ← takes from the front. Who is at the front, and how many are left?
scene.queues.front_last.objective: → adds to the back and ← takes from the front. Who is at the front, and who was the last to leave?
hint.queues.1: Write the queue down and update it after every step.
hint.queues.2: New items join at the back. Items always leave from the front.
hint.queues.3: The order never changes inside a queue. Only the ends move.
concept.queues.name: Queues
concept.queues.idea: A queue serves items in the order they arrived. First in, first out.
concept.queues.seen: Print jobs, task schedulers, breadth-first search, message brokers
place.bit_tricks.name: Bit tricks
scene.bit_tricks.popcount.objective: How many 1 bits does {n} have in binary?
scene.bit_tricks.power_of_two.objective: Is each number a power of two?
hint.bit_tricks.1: Write the number in binary first.
hint.bit_tricks.2: n − 1 flips the lowest 1 bit to 0 and every 0 below it to 1.
hint.bit_tricks.3: So n & (n − 1) removes the lowest 1 bit. A power of two has exactly one 1 bit, so the result is 0.
concept.bit_tricks.name: Bit manipulation
concept.bit_tricks.idea: n & (n − 1) clears the lowest set bit. Repeating it counts the 1 bits; a result of 0 means a power of two.
concept.bit_tricks.seen: Counting set bits, checking powers of two, permission masks, fast hashes
reveal.bit_tricks: You used the lowest bit to do the counting.
place.sorting.name: Sorting
scene.sorting.bubble.objective: Sort the row, smallest first. You can only swap neighbours, {budget} swaps at most.
scene.sorting.any_swap.objective: Sort the row, smallest first. Swap any two tiles, {budget} swaps at most.
hint.sorting.1: Tap one tile, then another, to swap them.
hint.sorting.2: With neighbour swaps, every pair that is out of order needs one swap.
hint.sorting.3: With any swaps, put the smallest tile in place first, then the next smallest.
concept.sorting.name: Sorting by swaps
concept.sorting.idea: Neighbour swaps need one swap per out-of-order pair. Free swaps need one per tile, minus one per cycle.
concept.sorting.seen: Bubble sort and selection sort, counting inversions, measuring how unsorted data is
reveal.sorting: Sorted, with not a swap to spare.
place.hashing.name: Hashing
scene.hashing.bucket.objective: Which bucket does each key go to?
scene.hashing.collisions.objective: Keys go in one at a time. How many land in a bucket that is already taken?
scene.hashing.probing.objective: Keys go in one at a time. A full bucket sends a key to the next free one. Which bucket does {last} end up in?
hint.hashing.1: h(k) = k mod m: divide by m and keep the remainder.
hint.hashing.2: Work through the keys in order and keep track of which buckets are full.
hint.hashing.3: Linear probing tries the next bucket, wrapping from the last one back to 0.
concept.hashing.name: Hash tables
concept.hashing.idea: A hash turns a key straight into a bucket number, so lookups skip the search. Clashes still need handling.
concept.hashing.seen: Dictionaries and sets, database indexes, caches, load balancers
reveal.hashing: You found each bucket without searching.
place.recursion.name: Recursion
scene.recursion.value.objective: Work out the value from the rule.
scene.recursion.calls.objective: How many calls in total does fib({n}) make, the first call included?
hint.recursion.1: Start from the smallest case and build up.
hint.recursion.2: Write the values in a row: f(0), f(1), f(2)… each one uses the ones before it.
hint.recursion.3: For calls, each call adds 1 plus the calls its two children make.
concept.recursion.name: Recursion
concept.recursion.idea: A recursive rule defines a value from smaller values of itself, down to a base case.
concept.recursion.seen: Tree traversal, divide and conquer, parsing, why plain recursive fib is slow
reveal.recursion: You built it up from the base case.
place.sliding_window.name: Sliding window
scene.sliding_window.window.objective: Pick {k} neighbouring tiles with the biggest possible total.
hint.sliding_window.1: Every window has exactly {k} tiles next to each other.
hint.sliding_window.2: Moving the window one step adds one tile and drops one.
hint.sliding_window.3: Keep a running total and the best total so far as you slide.
concept.sliding_window.name: Sliding window
concept.sliding_window.idea: Slide a fixed-size window along the data, updating its total by one in, one out.
concept.sliding_window.seen: Moving averages, rate limits, longest substring problems, streaming data
reveal.sliding_window: You slid the window instead of starting over.
place.prefix_sums.name: Prefix sums
place.prefix_sums.tagline: Sum any range in one step
scene.prefix_sums.range.objective: What is the sum of this range?
scene.prefix_sums.from_prefix.objective: P holds running totals: P[i] is a[0] + … + a[i]. What is the sum of the range?
hint.prefix_sums.1: Add up the values from the first index to the last, both included.
hint.prefix_sums.2: P[j] is the total up to j. Take away everything before i.
hint.prefix_sums.3: The sum of a[i] … a[j] is P[j] − P[i − 1].
concept.prefix_sums.name: Prefix sums
concept.prefix_sums.idea: Store running totals once, then any range sum is one subtraction.
concept.prefix_sums.seen: Range queries, 2D image sums, analytics dashboards
place.greedy.name: Greedy choices
place.greedy.tagline: The best choice at each step
scene.greedy.meetings.objective: Book as many meetings as you can into one room. No two may overlap.
hint.greedy.1: A meeting that ends early leaves the most room for others.
hint.greedy.2: Sort by end time. Take the first, then the next one that starts after it ends.
hint.greedy.3: Meetings that touch, one ending at 5 and the next starting at 5, do not overlap.
concept.greedy.name: Greedy algorithms
concept.greedy.idea: Choosing the meeting that ends first, again and again, gives the most meetings.
concept.greedy.seen: Interval scheduling, coin change with friendly coins, Huffman codes
reveal.greedy: The earliest finish won each time.
place.heaps.name: Heaps
place.heaps.tagline: The smallest is always on top
scene.heaps.last_out.objective: + adds a number. − takes out the smallest. Which number does the last − take out?
scene.heaps.first_last.objective: + adds a number. − takes out the smallest. Which numbers come out first and last?
scene.heaps.top_size.objective: + adds a number. − takes out the smallest. What is on top at the end, and how many are left?
hint.heaps.1: Keep a list of what is inside and update it after each step.
hint.heaps.2: Each − removes the smallest number inside at that moment.
hint.heaps.3: The order numbers were added in does not matter, only their sizes.
concept.heaps.name: Heaps and priority queues
concept.heaps.idea: A min-heap always hands out its smallest item first, whatever order items arrived in.
concept.heaps.seen: Task scheduling, Dijkstra’s algorithm, top-k problems, event simulations
place.bfs.name: Breadth-first search
place.bfs.tagline: Spread out one step at a time
scene.bfs.fewest_steps.objective: Draw the shortest path from the orange dot to the ring. Dark cells are walls.
hint.bfs.1: Think about every cell you can reach in 1 step, then 2, then 3.
hint.bfs.2: Spreading out evenly in all directions reaches each cell by its shortest route first.
hint.bfs.3: Walls force detours. Count the steps of a few routes before you commit.
concept.bfs.name: Breadth-first search
concept.bfs.idea: Exploring level by level reaches every cell by the fewest steps.
concept.bfs.seen: Shortest paths in mazes and maps, social network distance, web crawlers
reveal.bfs: You took the fewest steps possible.
place.combinatorics.name: Combinatorics
scene.combinatorics.choose.objective: Work out the number of combinations.
scene.combinatorics.sweets.objective: Share {k} identical sweets between {n} children. Some may get none. How many ways are there?
scene.combinatorics.socks.objective: A drawer has socks in {c} colours. How many must you take, without looking, to be sure of {m} of one colour?
scene.combinatorics.divisible.objective: How many numbers from 1 to {n} divide by {a} or by {b}?
hint.combinatorics.1: Choosing k from n: C(n, k) = n! ÷ (k! × (n − k)!).
hint.combinatorics.2: Sweets: line them up and add dividers between children. Choose where the dividers go.
hint.combinatorics.3: Pigeonhole: think of the worst luck first. Divisible: count each, then take away the ones counted twice.
concept.combinatorics.name: Combinatorics
concept.combinatorics.idea: Clever counting: combinations, stars and bars, the pigeonhole principle and inclusion–exclusion.
concept.combinatorics.seen: Estimating search spaces, hashing collisions, probability, puzzle interviews
reveal.combinatorics: Counted without listing a single case.
place.dynamic_programming.name: Dynamic programming
scene.dynamic_programming.stairs.objecti: You climb {n} stairs, taking this many steps at a time. In how many different ways can you reach the top?
scene.dynamic_programming.coins.objectiv: Using these coins as often as you like, what is the fewest coins that make {amount}?
scene.dynamic_programming.grid_paths.obj: Move only right or down, avoiding ■. How many paths go from the top-left to the bottom-right?
hint.dynamic_programming.1: Answer the small cases first: 1 stair, 2 stairs, an amount of 1, the first row.
hint.dynamic_programming.2: Each answer is built from answers you already have.
hint.dynamic_programming.3: Stairs: add the ways from the steps below. Coins: 1 + the best for the amount minus each coin. Grid: add the cell above and the cell to the left.
concept.dynamic_programming.name: Dynamic programming
concept.dynamic_programming.idea: Store the answers to small cases and build bigger answers from them, so nothing is worked out twice.
concept.dynamic_programming.seen: Edit distance, route planning, coin change, many interview problems
reveal.dynamic_programming: You reused small answers to build the big one.
place.knapsack.name: Knapsack
scene.knapsack.bag.objective: Fill the bag up to {cap} kg with the highest total value.
hint.knapsack.1: The most valuable items are not always the best choice.
hint.knapsack.2: Look at value per kilogram, but check that the leftover space is not wasted.
hint.knapsack.3: Try swapping one item for two lighter ones and compare the totals.
concept.knapsack.name: The 0/1 knapsack
concept.knapsack.idea: Choosing items under a weight limit needs every combination weighed. Greedy picks can miss the best.
concept.knapsack.seen: Budget planning, resource allocation, cargo loading, ad selection
place.shortest_paths.name: Shortest paths
scene.shortest_paths.cheapest.objective: Draw the cheapest path from the orange dot to the ring. Each cell costs its number to enter.
hint.shortest_paths.1: The path with the fewest steps is not always the cheapest.
hint.shortest_paths.2: Go around expensive cells when the detour costs less.
hint.shortest_paths.3: Dijkstra’s algorithm always grows the cheapest path found so far.
concept.shortest_paths.name: Dijkstra’s algorithm
concept.shortest_paths.idea: Always extend the cheapest known path next. With no negative costs, that finds the cheapest route.
concept.shortest_paths.seen: Maps and navigation, network routing, game AI
place.topological_sort.name: Topological sort
scene.topological_sort.tasks.objective: Tap the tasks in an order that works. An arrow means the first task must come before the second.
hint.topological_sort.1: Start with a task that nothing points to.
hint.topological_sort.2: After doing a task, its arrows no longer count.
hint.topological_sort.3: Repeat: pick any task with no arrows still pointing at it.
concept.topological_sort.name: Topological sort
concept.topological_sort.idea: Ordering tasks so that every task comes after the ones it depends on.
concept.topological_sort.seen: Build systems, package managers, course planning, spreadsheet updates
reveal.topological_sort: Every task came after what it needed.
place.search_the_answer.name: Search the answer
scene.search_the_answer.ship.objective: Ship these parcels in this order within {days} days. What is the smallest daily limit that works?
scene.search_the_answer.isqrt.objective: What is the biggest whole number whose square is at most {n}?
hint.search_the_answer.1: Guess an answer and check whether it works.
hint.search_the_answer.2: If a limit works, every bigger limit works too, so binary search the answer.
hint.search_the_answer.3: The answer is at least the heaviest parcel and at most the total weight.
concept.search_the_answer.name: Binary search on the answer
concept.search_the_answer.idea: When bigger answers keep working once one does, you can binary search the answer itself.
concept.search_the_answer.seen: Capacity planning, square roots, splitting work evenly, many interview problems
reveal.search_the_answer: You searched the answer, not the data.
place.xor_tricks.name: XOR tricks
scene.xor_tricks.single.objective: Every number appears twice except one. Which one is alone?
scene.xor_tricks.swap.objective: Run the three lines. What are a and b at the end?
hint.xor_tricks.2: XOR is about bits: a column ends up 1 when an odd number of the picked tiles have a 1 there.
hint.xor_tricks.3: Pairs cancel each other out, so XOR of everything leaves the lone number.
concept.xor_tricks.name: XOR
concept.xor_tricks.idea: XOR cancels pairs: x ^ x = 0. That finds lone items, swaps values and checks parity.
concept.xor_tricks.seen: Finding the single number, RAID parity, checksums, simple encryption
place.union_find.name: Union–find
scene.union_find.groups.objective: People 1 to {n}. Each link joins two people into the same group. How many groups are there?
scene.union_find.groups_biggest.objectiv: People 1 to {n}. Each link joins two groups. How many groups are there, and how big is the biggest?
hint.union_find.1: Start with everyone in their own group.
hint.union_find.2: Each link merges two groups, unless they are already the same group.
hint.union_find.3: People with no links are groups of one.
concept.union_find.name: Union–find
concept.union_find.idea: Track groups by merging them as links arrive, without redrawing the whole picture.
concept.union_find.seen: Network connectivity, Kruskal’s spanning trees, friend circles, image regions
reveal.union_find: You merged the groups as the links came in.
place.probability.name: Probability
scene.probability.dice_sum.objective: You roll two dice. In how many of the 36 outcomes is the total {s}?
scene.probability.heads.objective: You flip {n} coins. How many outcomes have exactly {k} heads?
scene.probability.at_least_one_six.objec: You roll {n} dice. How many outcomes have at least one six?
hint.probability.1: List the ways in a small table, or count them.
hint.probability.2: Exactly k heads: choose which k coins are heads, C(n, k).
hint.probability.3: At least one: count all outcomes, then take away the ones with none.
concept.probability.name: Counting outcomes
concept.probability.idea: Probability is favourable outcomes divided by all outcomes, so count carefully.
concept.probability.seen: Randomised algorithms, testing, load estimates, hash collisions
place.caching.name: Caching
place.caching.tagline: What to keep, what to drop
scene.caching.lru.objective: A cache holds {cap} items and drops the least recently used. How many requests are misses?
scene.caching.fifo.objective: A cache holds {cap} items and drops the oldest one added. How many requests are misses?
hint.caching.1: A miss is a request for something not in the cache. Then it gets added.
hint.caching.2: When the cache is full, one item has to go first.
hint.caching.3: LRU: a hit makes an item fresh again. FIFO: hits change nothing.
concept.caching.name: Caching
concept.caching.idea: A cache keeps recent items close. The eviction rule decides how often you miss.
concept.caching.seen: CPU caches, browser caches, CDNs, database buffers
reveal.caching: You kept the right things in the cache.
place.rate_limiting.name: Load and limits
scene.rate_limiting.token_bucket.objecti: The bucket holds {cap} tokens, starts full and gains {rate} each second. Each request uses one. Requests per second are shown. How many get through?
scene.rate_limiting.round_robin.objectiv: {m} servers take requests in turn, starting with server 1. Which server gets request {n}?
scene.rate_limiting.least_loaded.objecti: Each job goes to whichever of the {servers} servers has the least work so far. How much work does the busiest server end up with?
hint.rate_limiting.1: Simulate it one second, or one job, at a time.
hint.rate_limiting.2: Round robin is a remainder: work out which turn of the cycle you are on.
hint.rate_limiting.3: Token bucket: requests beyond the tokens left are refused, and the bucket never holds more than its size.
concept.rate_limiting.name: Rate limiting and load balancing
concept.rate_limiting.idea: Token buckets smooth out bursts; round robin and least-loaded spread work across servers.
concept.rate_limiting.seen: API gateways, web servers, queues, cloud autoscaling
tip.answer: Tap a field, then enter your answer.
tip.probe: Drag along the line or use − and +, then check.
tip.route: Drag from the orange dot to the ring.
fail.probe.out_of_checks: Out of checks with more than one number left.
fail.pick.wrong_count: That is not the right number of tiles.
fail.pick.too_much: That adds up to too much.
fail.pick.too_little: That adds up to too little.
fail.pick.wrong_xor: Those tiles XOR to a different number.
fail.pick.not_together: A window has to be tiles next to each other.
fail.pick.not_best: That works, but a better choice exists.
fail.ops.wrong_order: Something came out in the wrong order.
fail.ops.too_many_moves: Sorted, but with more swaps than needed.
fail.ops.too_early: A task came before something it needs.
fail.route.unfinished: The path has to reach the ring.
fail.route.longer: That gets there, but a better path exists.
probe.bisect_note: Bad means the first bad one is here or earlier.
ui.locked_tier: Solve {count} more {tier} scenes to open this topic.
